messages.subject: GGIR version 1.5-1
messages.body_plain:
GGIR version 1.5-1 now online with a few important updates:

- A 'beta-version' functionality to read cwa-format files from Axivity has been added. Special thanks to Evgeny Mirkes from the University of Leicester for writing and sharing this code.
- Bug fixed in correct timestamp interpretation for GENEActiv data, which was accidentally introduced in August 2016. It has timestamps, but in the wrong timezone. This only affects GENEActiv data
- Other updates are listed here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html>

For those interested in seeing the underlying code and contributing: I copied the GGIR github repo from the ucl github organisation where it has lived for the past year to a new neutral github organisation I recently created: https://github.com/wadpac.

For the latest overview of GGIR related publications see here <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/wiki/Publication-list>. Please email me when you spot a new publication that is not on the list yet.

Thanks, Vincent

messages.subject: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
messages.subject_clean: How to select specific hours in an analysis ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have one week of accelerometer data for my participants, strictly starting on Tuesday (16 pm) and finishing on Sunday (23:59 pm) for each participant.

I would like to compute physical activity scores representing mean physical activity performed from Tuesday to Friday only in the evening, precisely between 17 pm and sleep (an arbitrary threshold such as 23:59 pm could also be suitable),

How can I do that ? Vincent tell me that it is in the g.part5 but even with this information I can't solve this problem,

Thanks in advance for your help, as well as the development and maintenance of this package,

Cheers !

Guillaume

messages.subject: Combination of Sleep Log and Accelerometer Sleep Detection?
messages.subject_clean: Combination of Sleep Log and Accelerometer Sleep Detection?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I thought I read that if the relyonsleeplog is set to TRUE then GGIR will defer to the sleep log for bed times and wake times - And if bed times or wake times in the sleep log are missing, GGIR will determine these based on the accelerometer detection. However, the night summary output is removing the nights with no corresponding sleep log information (all nights are sleeplog_used = TRUE).

Is there a specification to include the sleep log first, then defer to accelerometer detection second so that all nights can be included?

Thanks for the input!
- Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Combination of Sleep Log and Accelerometer Sleep Detection?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Combination of Sleep Log and Accelerometer Sleep Detection?
messages.body_plain:
What you want is already stored by default in the QC folder, which is inside the results folder.
The csv you are looking at ends with _cleaned in the file name and is a tidied up version with only 'valid' nights (depending on what criteria you specified.
The csv in the QC folder shows you all the nights and leaves it up to you to decide which nights you want to keep or through away. The package documentation should clarify variables like 'cleaningcode' which you will need in the process of cleaning the data to your own liking.

The argument relyonsleeplog means that you do not trust the accelerometer data for detecting sleep onset and waking time. This is only a realistic scenario if you instructed your participants to take the accelerometer off during the night. In all other case, my advise is to leave argument relyonsleeplog to its default FALSE.

messages.body_plain:
Thank you Vincent! I overlooked the full file.

Also, can you provide some insight on how GGIR processes the sleep date-time? Does it pull the date from the start date-time-stamp of the accelerometer, since the sleep log has no date stamp?

For example, I have a large sample of participants that were given the accelerometer on say, Wednesday and instructed to not record their bed time that night, but to instead record their wake time and bed time on Thursday. Some recorded the Wednesday bed time anyways, resulting in a "first night" that really shouldn't scored. Others completed the log correctly, so their "first night" would be Thursday night.

I've come up with 3 possible scenarios:
1. Use full night summary, include first and last nights, and delete night 1
    - correctly filled sleep logs (first night not logged, second night logged as first) will result in incorrectly advancing sleep log by 1 date
2. Delay the start by 12 hours - skips first 12 hours (night) of data, treats first sleep log entry as night 1
    - incorrectly filled sleep logs (first night logged as first night) will result in incorrectly pushing back sleep log by 1 date
3. Insert blank sleep log entry if actigraphy start date is 1 calendar date less than first sleep log entry to create a false first night sleep log entry

Would you agree with these results based on how GGIR reads the sleep log time-stamps?
For our analyses, we'd like to consider the entire sleep window - between sleep log bed time and sleep log wake time.

Thank you!
- Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: GGIR version 1.5-1
messages.body_plain:
I have uploaded GGIR version 1.5-3 with some bug fixes last night, introduced in version 1.5-1 I uploaded last week.

If you are working in Windows then please wait a couple of days as Windows binaries need to be compiled by CRAN before they become active.

Error messages that should be resolved now:
- Error in Math.factor(Xi) : ‘cumsum’ not meaningful for factors
- Error in Rcpp::sourceCpp("src/numUnpack.cpp") : file not found: 'V:/Axivity/R/src/numUnpack.cpp'
- Error in g.readaccfile(filename = datafile, blocksize = blocksize, blocknumber = i,  :  object 'P' not found".
- Error in as.matrix(deci$rawxyz) : object 'deci' not found => in relation to g.wavread

Additionally, I have made a start with building a package vignette to offers new users a speed course in using GGIR: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html.
I am aware that this needs further improvement, but if you have tips on what should be in there or want to contribute yourself, then please get in touch.

I also added some contributing guidelines at https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR

Thanks, and sorry for the inconvenience the recent bugs may have caused.

Vincent

On 23 April 2017 at 15:56, Vincent van Hees <vincent...@gmail.com> wrote:
> GGIR version 1.5-1 now online with a few important updates:
>
> - A 'beta-version' functionality to read cwa-format files from Axivity has been added. Special thanks to Evgeny Mirkes from the University of Leicester for writing and sharing this code.
> - Bug fixed in correct timestamp interpretation for GENEActiv data, which was accidentally introduced in August 2016. It has timestamps, but in the wrong timezone. This only affects GENEActiv data
> - Other updates are listed here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html>
>
> For those interested in seeing the underlying code and contributing: I copied the GGIR github repo from the ucl github organisation where it has lived for the past year to a new neutral github organisation I recently created: https://github.com/wadpac.
>
> For the latest overview of GGIR related publications see here <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/wiki/Publication-list>. Please email me when you spot a new publication that is not on the list yet.
>
> Thanks, Vincent
>
